## Motivating Question

When a body with constant heat capacity $C$ at initial temperature $T_0$ is placed in contact with a sequence of $N$ thermal reservoirs at equally spaced temperatures $T_k = T_0 + k\,\Delta T$ up to $T_N$, how rapidly does the total entropy variation

$$\frac{\Delta S_{\text{tot}}(N)}{C} = \sum_{k=1}^{N} \left( \frac{T_{k-1}}{T_k} - 1 + \ln\frac{T_k}{T_{k-1}} \right)$$

decay as $N \to \infty$?

## Asymptotic Expansion vs. Precomputed Finite-$N$ Sum

Expanding each step to second order in $\Delta T / T_k$ shows that $\Delta S_{\text{tot}}(N) / C = \mathcal{O}(N^{-1})$ as $N \to \infty$, recovering thermodynamic reversibility in the quasi-static continuum limit ([Freitas & Pereira 2019](https://doi.org/10.1590/1806-9126-rbef-2018-0331)).
